_comment: What each non-conforming fixture is for. `schemaValid` drives the schema conformance run; `readerAccepts` is asserted by the M2 validator, because the reader is deliberately more permissive than the schema in the ways docs/SPEC.md sections 6 and 7 name.

missing-format.json.why: format is required, and a reader must never guess at a file's type

wrong-format.json.why: format must be the literal tabspack

missing-schema-version.json.why: schemaVersion is required so a reader knows which rules apply

windows-not-array.json.why: windows is an array, never an id keyed object

tab-without-url.json.why: url is the only mandatory field on a tab

unknown-group-color.json.why: the schema pins the colour list, but SPEC section 6 tells a reader to fall back to grey rather than fail the import

index-not-integer.json.why: index is an integer; a reader rounds or reorders rather than losing the tab

truncated.json.why: not JSON at all, so the failure must name the byte offset

future-version.tabspack.json.why: schema cannot express a version gate. A v1 reader must refuse version 2 by name rather than parse it badly

dangling-group-ref.tabspack.json.why: reference integrity is not expressible in JSON Schema. The reader drops the dangling reference and reports it

two-active-tabs.tabspack.json.why: SPEC section 5: a reader honours the first active tab and ignores the rest

duplicate-index.tabspack.json.why: duplicate indices are resolved by array order, and reindexed on import

restricted-urls.tabspack.json.why: five URLs no extension can open. They must be listed on the placeholder page and counted, never dropped silently
